plain_description.what: Scores the label-free intent trees on two intent datasets (MASSIVE, CLINC) against their gold class hierarchy, giving credit at every node, not just leaves. It compares them with average-link clustering and with 200 random trees of the same shape. No judge calls.
plain_description.why: It asks whether the tree captures the true hierarchy above its leaves, which is the point of building a tree rather than flat clusters.
plain_description.information: Beating random same-shape trees would show the tree carries hierarchy beyond its leaves. Result: done. The tree scores far above average-link on both corpora (0.75 and 0.85 against 0.27 and 0.34), but average-link degenerated into one huge leaf, so this means 'better than a broken baseline', not 'better than a competent hierarchy'. The comparison with random trees could not be evaluated as designed (impossible on CLINC). On MASSIVE alone it is above random, as a per-corpus descriptive reading only.
